host.performance_cores: 0-15 capped at 2.2 GHz since 2026-10-23 (untimed work only)

choices.note: Efficiency core: CPU 16 (Gracemont), one thread, under the shared lock after the quiet-host check, 4,096 arguments in cache, the least time per element. Performance core: CPU 5 (Golden Cove, capped at 2.2 GHz since 2026-10-23), untimed, for comparison only. Ranges: tiny log-uniform (1e-300, 1e-5), unit (1e-5, 3), moderate (3, 100), large log-uniform (100, 1e300), nb y + 1/alpha (y geometric, mean 20; alpha log-uniform 1e-8 to 1e3), negative (-1, 0), exp_small (-1, 1), exp_wide (-700, 700). max_ulp: 10^6 arguments per range against long double references. These historical slow-policy choices were made on the efficiency cores; the division_modes section records the subsequent Zen 3 selection, and they issue about one 256-bit division per 32 cycles.

log.reason: Current AVX2 wins over the earlier division-based algorithm; scalar glibc remains faster.

log1p.engine_scalar: glibc and existing stable log-ratio expression
log1p.engine_array: earlier division-based log1p in edgeR deviances
log1p.reason: Earlier AVX2 is faster on Zen 3, within 1 ulp; scalar glibc is faster than either own scalar kernel.
log1p.boost_double_check: Measured in exclusive Slurm job 657, two rounds, five ranges. The Boost wrapper delegates to glibc and is slower or tied. Raw times and errors: DIVISION_CHOICES.json boost_log1p_check.

exp.reason: Current AVX2 wins; there is no separate earlier exp algorithm.

lgamma.vmath_array: earlier own positive kernel, libm for negative values
lgamma.reason: Earlier AVX2 wins over glibc; glibc wins scalar calls.

digamma.reason: Fastest eligible array implementation. Combined recurrence exceeds accuracy bound. Boost double wins scalar repeated and dependent calls after fair FMA inlining.

trigamma.reason: Boost-derived FMA rational wins dependent-call microbenchmarks, but is 1.5% slower on edgeR QL and gives no bulk-DE gain in paired end-to-end measurements. Keep Boost double at engine call sites. Faster rational AVX2 exceeds the tighter standalone API accuracy bound.

sleef_attempt.note: The first 1.5.0 backend: SLEEF 3.9.0 u10 (AVX2, Advanced SIMD, scalar FMA) for log, log1p, exp and lgamma, removed. Efficiency-core timings (CPU 16, one thread, under the lock) against the 1.4.1 base; its log, log1p and lgamma divide (double-double arithmetic), and Gracemont issues about one 256-bit division per 32 cycles. Performance-core figures are untimed (CPU 5, capped at 2.2 GHz).
